data.gender_notes: Elimas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Elimas comes from the Hebrew language, derived from the elements 'El' (God) and 'mas' (my). This name was borne by several characters in the Old Testament, most notably a priest in the Book of Malachi and a Levite in the Book of Chronicles. In both cases, Elimas is shown to be a devoted servant of God, dedicating his life to the service of the Temple.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of deep faith and devotion.
data.etymology: Elimas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “My El God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Elimas total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.spiritual_significance: The name Elimas represents a deep connection to God and obedience to His will. Its origins emphasize the importance of faith and devotion to the Almighty, making it a spiritual name with a powerful reminder to always keep God at the center of one's life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Elimas may symbolize God's solace and strength in times of hardship. The name derives from the Hebrew "El," meaning God, and "Mas," meaning relief or deliverance. In the Old Testament, Elim is a place where God provided water and rest for the Israelites, reflecting the spiritual sustenance and refuge this name offers.

He is known for his dramatic showdowns with the prophets of the pagan god Baal and for his ascent into heaven in a chariot of fire.

Elias, also known as Alias or Elimelech, was a Hebrew man mentioned in the Book of Ruth, which is set in the time of the Judges in the 12th or 13th century BCE. He and his family left Bethlehem due to a famine and moved to Moab, where his two sons married Moabite women.
